relatedSnapshot.title: Answer prospects who send their own scheduling link, and hand the booking to the host
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

This is part 3 of ENG-14785. When a prospect sends their own scheduling link, the AI SDR replies straight away, the way a person would, and the host gets a one-click task to book it. Today those prospects get no reply at all, which is the worst outcome for someone who's ready to book.

## Problem

* Since ENG-11624, a prospect's own link sends the thread to a person and the AI says nothing. That happened 78 times in 4 weeks.
* An earlier design, ENG-11714, set the rule we keep here: only reply once the task for the host really exists.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Prospect sends own link] --> B[NEW: create host task]
  B -- task created --> C[NEW: instant reply sent]
  B -- task fails --> D[Hand-off, as today]
  C --> E[Host books their link]
  E --> F[Booking stops follow-ups]
```

## What's included

1. **Keep the link as data.** Store the prospect's link on the thread, not only inside a text reason.
2. **Create the host task.** The task goes to the campaign host. If there's no host, it goes to the deal owner, then the workspace owner. It carries:
   * the link;
   * two times the host is free;
   * a due time 2 business hours away.

   The host also gets an in-app notification.
3. **Send the reply.** Only once the task and the notification both exist, the AI replies: "Perfect, I'll grab a time on your calendar." It never names a time. If either step fails, hand the thread to a person as today, and send nothing.
4. **While the task is open,** the AI sends no follow-ups. If no booking appears after one business day, remind the host.
5. **When the booking appears on the host calendar,** the detection from ENG-14786 marks the thread booked and the task closes itself.

## Out of scope

* Booking through the prospect's link automatically.
* Sending our own link, which is a separate change.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14786.

## Done when

* A prospect who sends a Calendly or <domain> link gets the reply, and the host gets the task and the notification. How to check: an end-to-end run in preview.
* When task creation fails, no reply is sent and the thread goes to a person. How to check: an integration test.
* When the host books, the thread turns booked and the task closes.
* No follow-up sends while the task is open.

## Implementation context

* Today's hand-off: `PROSPECT_PROVIDED_SCHEDULING_LINK` in booking.ts, around lines 281 to 287.
* The booking-validation prompt already recognises a prospect's own link.
* Free times come from ENG-14760's shared slot function if it has merged. Otherwise, use slot matching's no-preference path.
* Full detail: AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR smart-followup treats a shared scheduling/Calendly link as a booked meeting → drops warm leads from reminders
relatedSnapshot.description:
Source: Raindrop CRITICAL issue Shared scheduling links treated as booked meetings (75 events, 58 users, 7d). Surfaced in the Jul 12 2026 Raindrop Daily Summary. Validated independently by the Raindrop Alert Processor.

## Symptom

When a prospect shares their OWN scheduling link (Calendly/calendar) or asks the sender to schedule, the `smart-followup` agent (`google/gemini-2.5-flash`, agent_id `<uuid>`, prompt v2) sets `requires_followup: false` and ends the sequence, citing a successful booking. No meeting time was ever confirmed, so an interested lead is silently dropped from the reminder sequence.

## Root cause (verified in code)

`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/agents/smart-followup/default-agent.ts` — the system prompt's "Name 2 are NOT Required" list (lines 17-22) includes:

```
- Meeting was successfully booked (calendar handles reminders)
```

There is no guidance distinguishing a confirmed slot from (a) a prospect sharing their own scheduling link, or (b) a "you go ahead and book it" handoff. The model equates any link-based scheduling gesture with a completed booking. Matches Raindrop's root-cause hypothesis exactly.

## Firsthand evidence

Event `<uuid>` (convo `<uuid>`, podcast campaign). Prospect merely sent their calendar link; agent output:

```json
{"requires_followup":false,"next_follow_up_date_iso":null,"followup_sequence":[],"reason":"Meeting was successfully booked (prospect sent their calendar link) - no follow-up needed."}
```

Corroborating stumbles today: agent cancels follow-up after prospect shares scheduling link, assistant ignored the user's booking link after saying Understood.

## Trend (adversarial note)

Issue-matched events peaked Jul 9 (25/day) and declined through Jul 11 (5/day); the headline "58 users" is a 7-day cumulative, not a single-day spike. Still real and recurring (today's stumbles confirm). Impact is high because the failure is silent — a genuinely interested lead is dropped with no reminder and no human flag.

## Suggested fix direction

In the smart-followup prompt, explicitly state that a shared scheduling link or a "you book it" handoff is NOT a confirmed booking and DOES require a follow-up (treat like "slots proposed, no confirmation"). Only suppress follow-ups when a specific time is confirmed. Overlaps with the broader prompt rework in ENG-8385; predecessor ENG-6398 (copywriter booking-link confusion) was canceled.

Owner via git blame: prompt block authored by Koppany Kondricz.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR booking-validation blocks prospect-provided scheduling links as NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT → reply re-offers manual slots
relatedSnapshot.description:
Source: Raindrop issue Booking replies ignore prospect scheduling links (23 events, 17 users, 7d; first seen Jul 7). Surfaced in the Jul 14 2026 Raindrop Daily Summary (Theme 3 + Painful convos 2 & 4). Validated independently by the Raindrop Alert Processor.

This is the **live-reply counterpart** to ENG-11508 (smart-followup, fixed in #5507). ENG-11508 stopped scheduling-link leads from being silently dropped from follow-ups; this ticket is the *drafted reply* still ignoring the link. ENG-6398 (canceled Mar 2026) described the same class of copywriter/booking-link confusion.

## Symptom

When an interested prospect shares their OWN scheduling link (Calendly/calendar) in a booking thread, the `booking-validation` agent classifies the message as `NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT` and blocks the booking. The workflow then routes to the copywriter, which re-offers manual time slots (or asks the prospect for times) — ignoring the link the prospect provided to end the back-and-forth. Prolongs threads with the warmest, most ready-to-book leads and compounds into AI-identification escalations (Theme 4).

## Root cause (verified in code)

`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/agents/booking-validation/default-agent.ts` — the Name 3 system prompt only recognizes two outcomes: (a) prospect confirms a specific *offered/proposed* time → `can_book: true`, or (b) everything else → blocked. There is **no branch** for "prospect supplied their own scheduling link / delegated booking." Such a message has no specific slot, so the model falls into the "General Interest / no specific time" bucket and returns `NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT`.

`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/agents/booking-validation/helpers.ts` — `bookingBlockingCategorySchema` has no category for a prospect-provided link (`NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT | MISSING_REQUIRED_INFO | TIME_NOT_PREVIOUSLY_OFFERED | SLOTS_NOT_YET_OFFERED | OTHER`).

`apps/web/lib/ai-sdr-v2/workflow/steps/booking.ts` (L180-235) — on `!can_book`, the step emits the `ai_sdr_booking_blocked_no_specific_slot` signal and hands off to the offer-alternatives/copywriter path, which drafts a manual-slot reply. The copywriter is never told a prospect link is present or how to handle it.

Raindrop's root-cause hypothesis ("copywriter follows the routed directive over the latest inbound message") points at the copywriter, but the decision that discards the link is upstream in booking-validation.

## Firsthand evidence (2 confirmed events, both parsed cleanly — NOT the GENERATION_ERROR/ENG-10838 storm)

* Event `<uuid>` (convo `e4758741...`, podcast; prospect Name 4), booking-validation, gemini-2.5-flash, `used_fallback:false`, `status:success`:
  `{"can_book":false,"blocking_category":"NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT","blocking_reason":"Prospect is asking the SDR to book a time using their calendar link, not confirming a specific time slot..."}`
* Event `<uuid>` (convo `f41d15d3...`, Painful convo 4; prospect Name 5 shared Calendly twice), same agent/model/success:
  `{"can_book":false,"blocking_category":"NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT","blocking_reason":"Prospect is providing a Calendly link, not confirming a specific time..."}`

## Name 6 notes

* Raindrop attributes `affected_dimensions` to `default-copywriter-scorer`/gemini and `get_issue_events` returns copywriter-scorer events — this is a **misattribution**: the scorer runs on every reply so it is overrepresented in matched events. The real failure is in booking-validation + copywriter.
* Volume is modest (23 ev / 17 users / 7d, ~1-3/day) and recurring all week — but every affected prospect is a warm, ready-to-book lead, so the business impact is disproportionate to the raw count. The umbrella signal `cc1e607f` (all NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT blocks, 356 today) is mostly legitimate "sounds good, no time" blocks; this bug is the scheduling-link subset.

## Suggested fix direction

* Detect a prospect-supplied scheduling link (or "you book it" delegation) in booking-validation and route it to a dedicated outcome instead of `NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT` — e.g. a new blocking category / directive that tells the copywriter to acknowledge the link and either (a) proceed to book via that link if the product supports it, or (b) reply agreeing to use it rather than re-offering manual slots. Mirror the distinction ENG-11508 added to smart-followup (shared link ≠ confirmed booking, but also ≠ "no specific time, re-offer slots").

Owner via git blame: booking-validation prompt authored primarily by Koppany Kondricz (69 lines); consistent owner of AI SDR scheduling/agent prompts.

relatedSnapshot.title: Prospects never receive the promised calendar invite or join link
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

After the AI SDR confirms a meeting time and tells the prospect an invite or Zoom link is coming shortly, the invite never arrives. Prospects write back saying it never came — sometimes even after a resend — or show up on the day with no link and have to reschedule. The Raindrop issue has been steady at 22 users over 7 days, so it's a standing leak in booked-meeting delivery, not a spike.

## What should happen

When the SDR commits to sending an invite/link, the calendar invite (with working join link) should actually go out — or the SDR should stop promising it. Needs investigation into whether the failure is in invite creation, email delivery, or link generation.

## Who it hits

22 users over 7 days (steady). Confirmed — Raindrop issue verified.

## Done when

- [ ] Every booking the SDR confirms results in a sent calendar invite with a working join link
- [ ] Failure to send an invite is surfaced (alert/flag) instead of discovered by the prospect
- [ ] Root cause identified: invite creation, delivery, or link generation

<details><summary>Engineering detail</summary>

* Raindrop issue: <url> (22 events / 22 users / 7d, first seen 2026-10-11, still firing today)
* Detected on `jev-auto-message-detection` decisions — prospect messages saying the invite never arrived
* Possibly related: ENG-15680 (appointment extraction writes unconfirmed meetings) and ENG-14761 (rebooks lost meetings)

</details>

Found via Raindrop digest 2026-10-20. Not reproduced yet.

relatedSnapshot.title: Handle "here's my Calendly link" replies: acknowledge + one-click human booking (stop re-offering slots)
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Review corrections (2026-07-16)

These notes supersede any conflicting implementation language below.

Correct the impact statement to about 38 affected threads/day and about 21 stalled threads/day at the stated 54.7% rate. Do not send "we will grab a time shortly" unless a durable, assigned booking task and client notification were successfully created. Store the scheduler URL as structured data, not only inside a reason string.

---

## Overview

When a warm prospect replies "just grab a time on my calendar: calendly.com/...", the AI completely ignores the link and offers its own time slots instead. The prospect told us exactly how to book the meeting and we talk past them, about 38 affected threads per day, with about 21 stalling at the stated rate. Decision (James, 2026-07-16): phase 1 is acknowledge the link and hand the client a one-click booking handoff. The AI booking directly on their link is a later phase with its own plan; do NOT build that here.

## The prod data (14 days)

* 534 threads blocked on the exact message where the prospect shared their own scheduler link (calendly.com 457, "my calendar" 222, <domain> 15).
* 54.7% of those stalled; 242 still sit in slots_sent, 183 of them very_high interest.
* Real example (redacted): prospect: "those timings unfortunately don't work. Here's G***'s calendar... you can lock it in calendly.com/g***/30min" → the AI re-offered 3 NEW manual times → thread stalled.
* IMPORTANT first step: a Raindrop signal `booking_blocked_prospect_scheduling_link` was created 2026-07-15 with 0 occurrences. Check whether that instrumentation shipped and simply never fires, or someone already started this work. Do not duplicate in-flight work.

## Root cause (verified in code)

A repo-wide grep finds calendly/<domain> awareness ONLY in the smart-followup prompt (follow-up timing hints, `agents/smart-followup/default-agent.ts:27`). The data-extraction agent is a "Time Preference Extractor" with no link concept in prompt or schema (`agents/data-extraction/default-agent.ts:3`), so a link-only reply yields zero time preferences; slot-matchmaking takes the no-preference branch and proposes 3 manual slots (`steps/slot-matchmaking.ts:314-368`); the reply-directive vocabulary (`workflow/helpers/context-pack-helpers/reply-directive.ts:53-137`) has exactly five outcomes (CONFIRM_BOOKING, OFFER_ALTERNATIVES x2, PRESENT_SLOTS, ASK_FOR_PREFERENCES), none of which can express "use their link"; the booking validator then blocks NO_SPECIFIC_SLOT.

## What to build (exactly this, one PR)

1. Deterministic URL detection in the data-normalizer or data-extraction step (code regex, NOT the LLM): calendly.com, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, appt.link, plus a generic "book/schedule a meeting" + URL heuristic. Expose as a structured field `prospect_scheduler_link` on the workflow state.
2. New reply directive ACTION `ACKNOWLEDGE_SCHEDULER_LINK`: instruction "Tell the prospect you will grab a time on their calendar shortly. Do NOT offer your own time slots. Do NOT confirm a specific time." Wire it into `generateBookingDirective` so it takes precedence over PRESENT_SLOTS/OFFER_ALTERNATIVES when the link flag is set.
3. Escalate to the client under a NEW escalation reason (e.g. `SCHEDULER_LINK_BOOKING('link')` in `constants/escalation-reasons.ts`) that includes the URL, so the client can book in one click. This must be its own category, not mixed into existing buckets.
4. Emit the existing `booking_blocked_prospect_scheduling_link` Raindrop signal from this path (or fix it if it exists but never fires).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the sample Calendly threads produces an acknowledge reply, not a slot re-offer
- [ ] Escalation carries the link and its own reason category
- [ ] The Raindrop signal fires in prod
- [ ] Stalled rate on scheduler-link threads measurably drops from the 54.7% baseline (check after 2 weeks)

relatedSnapshot.title: Integrate booking links properly into the AI SDR
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Let the AI SDR handle booking links both ways: send the host's link when a prospect asks, and answer prospects who send their own. We're doing this so more interested prospects book a meeting, and so nothing gives away that a machine is writing.

About 44 prospects a week ask the AI SDR for a booking link, and today it has none to send, so it offers times again. Those threads book within 7 days only 40.5% of the time on podcast campaigns and 28.1% on direct, against 87.5% when a prospect picks one of our times.

## Problem

Three things go wrong today, and each child fixes one. The diagram shows where.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Prospect asks for link] --> B["(2) Reply: link and times"]
  C[Prospect sends own link] --> D["(3) Reply and host task"]
  B --> E[Prospect or host books]
  D --> E
  E --> F["(1) Booking stops follow-ups"]
```

Each number is the child that changes that step.

1. A booking only stops follow-ups when Company One or EmailBison also marked the lead "interested", and a follow-up can go out before the calendar update arrives. One follow-up after a booking shows the prospect that a machine is writing.
2. The AI SDR has no booking link to send, even though 22% of active AI SDR workspaces keep one in their knowledge base.
3. When a prospect sends their own scheduling link, the thread goes to a person and the prospect gets no reply. That happened 78 times in 4 weeks.

## User experience

* A prospect who asks for our calendar gets the host's link with two times, in one reply.
* A prospect who sends their own link hears back within minutes, and the host gets a one-click task to book it.
* Whoever books, and however they book, follow-ups stop straight away and the thread shows as booked.
* Workspace owners see a new "Booking link" field on each meeting type.

## What's included

1. Stop follow-ups once a prospect books through any tool.
2. Let the AI SDR send the host's booking link.
3. Answer prospects who send their own scheduling link, and hand the booking to the host.

## Out of scope

* A direct Calendly integration (connecting Calendly, moving deals from it, and letting the AI SDR book through it): that's a separate master.
* Booking through a prospect's link with browser automation, because it's too error-prone for about 20 threads a week.
* Our own hosted booking page.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Waves show the earliest point a ticket can start, not a barrier.

### Wave 1: can start now

1. ENG-14786: stop follow-ups once a prospect books through any tool.

### Wave 2: starts when ENG-14786 is done

Parallel: ENG-14788 and ENG-14789. They both touch the reply-instruction code, so agree who changes it first.

2. ENG-14788: send the host's booking link. Blocked by ENG-14786.
3. ENG-14789: answer prospects' own links. Blocked by ENG-14786.

Cross-wave overlap: none.

## How we'll measure

* **Link asks that book.** Base: AI SDR threads where the prospect asked for our calendar or booking link, booked within 7 days, from the follow-up results report. Today it's 40.5% on podcast campaigns and 28.1% on direct. We'll aim toward the 87.5% of prospects who pick an offered time. We'll read it 4 weeks after the second child ships.
* **Follow-ups sent after a booking.** Base: follow-ups sent while the thread had a booking on the host calendar, from the first child's cancel log. Target: zero once it ships. We can't count today's value, because nothing logs it yet.

## Done when

* All three children are merged and released.
* The link-ask booking rate is posted on this ticket 4 weeks after the second child ships.

## Implementation context

* Research and plan: Booking Links and Calendly.
* Replaces ENG-14779, which is marked a duplicate of this ticket.
* Related: ENG-14756 (follow-ups v2), ENG-14760 (live times in follow-ups), ENG-14761 (rebook lost meetings), ENG-11624 (today's hand-off for prospects' own links), ENG-11714 (the earlier design for the reply to a prospect's own link), ENG-12059 (call length mismatch).

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR booking links: send ours, handle the prospect's own, and stop follow-ups the moment anyone books
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Three changes so booking feels human:

1. The AI SDR can send the host's own booking link (Calendly, <domain>, HubSpot or any link) when a prospect asks for one, and offer it as an "or book here" option next to times.
2. When a prospect sends *their* scheduling link, the AI replies straight away like a person would, and the host gets a one-click task to book it.
3. Whenever a prospect books through any tool, follow-ups stop. A follow-up after someone has booked is the clearest sign that a machine is writing, so this part ships first.

## Problem

* **About 44 prospects a week ask for our booking link.** The AI has no link to send, so it offers times again. Those threads book 40% (podcast) and 28% (direct) of the time, against 88% when a prospect picks one of our times. Most workspaces already have a link: one sits in the knowledge base for 60% of podcast threads and 35% of direct threads.
* **When a prospect sends their own scheduling link, nobody answers them.** Since ENG-11624 the AI escalates the thread to the client (78 runs in 4 weeks). It sends the prospect nothing, and escalated warm threads usually sit unanswered for days.
* **Follow-ups can still go out after someone books.** We already watch the host's Name 9 or Outlook calendar and cancel follow-ups when a prospect's booking appears (158 follow-ups cancelled in the last 28 days). It has two gaps:
  * the follow-up can be sent before the calendar update arrives;
  * the rule depends on Company One or EmailBison marking the lead "interested". That mark is present for about 94% of replied threads, so the other 6% are missed, and so is any provider that doesn't send it.

## User experience

**Workspace owner (settings):**

* Each meeting type gets an optional **Booking link** field. A campaign can override it, for teams where each host has their own link.
* If the knowledge base already contains a scheduler link, the field shows it as a suggestion. It is never filled in silently.

**Prospect asks for a link:** "Can you just send me your calendar?"

* The AI replies with the link, plus the times it would have offered.
* It never says it can't send a link.

**Prospect is offered times:** after the times, one line: "Or if it's easier, grab any time here: <link>". This line is tested 50/50 by thread (see Open questions).

**Prospect sends their own link:** "Just grab a time here: calendly.com/…"

* The AI replies within minutes: "Perfect, I'll grab a time on your calendar." It never names a time.
* At the same moment, the host gets a CRM task and a notification: "<Prospect> asked you to book via their link", with the link and two times the host is free.
* When the booking appears on the host's calendar, the thread is marked booked and the task closes itself.
* If the task is still open after one business day, the host gets a reminder. The AI sends no follow-ups while this is waiting.

**Prospect books by any route** (our link, their link, a forwarded invite): follow-ups stop, the booking shows on the thread, and the follow-up row records why it was cancelled.

## What's included

Two pull requests on this ticket, in this order.

**PR 1: stop follow-ups once anyone books. Ships first, no prospect-facing change.**

1. **Match on our own data, not the provider's label.** In the calendar-sync booking detection, a calendar attendee counts as a prospect booking when *either* of these holds:
   * the existing provider evidence (a reply plus an "interested" event);
   * **or** the prospect has sent us at least one real reply (not an auto-reply) in an AI SDR thread in this workspace. Any reply counts: interested, question, objection or not-now.
2. **Check right before each follow-up sends:**
   * Look for a booking with this prospect: our own appointments and tracked external bookings, plus a live look at the host's connected calendar for the next 60 days.
   * If the prospect, or another attendee from the same company email domain, is on an event created since our first reply in the thread, cancel the follow-up as `already_booked_external`.
   * Never match on shared mail domains such as gmail.com or outlook.com.
3. **Outcome logging:** every cancel records which check caught it, so we can see how much each part helps.

**PR 2: booking links**

4. **Booking link setting:** on meeting types, with a campaign override. https only, checked on save.
5. **Reply path:**
   * **Prospect asks for a link:** send the link and offer times. The writer can only insert the link as a code-filled placeholder and never types the URL itself.
   * **Fallback line next to offered times:** on for half of new threads (stable by thread), off for the other half.
6. **Follow-up writer:** allow `{{LINK:booking}}` in follow-ups. Use it in the "times passed" follow-up and whenever the prospect asked for a link. This needs one line in prompt v3 and an allowed-links entry.
7. **Prospect's own link:**
   * Replace today's escalation with three things: the acknowledgement reply, the host task with the link and two free times, and the notification.
   * Only send the reply once the task and the notification have both been created. If either fails, escalate as today and send nothing.
   * Keep the link as structured data on the thread, not only in a text reason.
8. **Activation tracking:** the new booking-link setting gets PostHog events through the repo's `instrument-activation-tracking` skill.

**Not included:**

* booking through the prospect's link by browser automation (too error-prone for about 20 threads a week);
* a direct Calendly connection (later, if links prove they book more);
* our own hosted booking page.

## Done when

- [ ] PR 1: a prospect who books through any tool on the host's connected calendar has every pending follow-up cancelled, including when the sending tool never marked them "interested" (integration test plus one preview run).
- [ ] PR 1: a follow-up due 1 minute after a booking lands is cancelled by the pre-send check, not sent (integration test).
- [ ] PR 1: an attendee from the same company domain cancels follow-ups; a gmail.com attendee does not (unit tests).
- [ ] PR 2: with a booking link set, "can you send me your calendar?" gets the link plus times. With no link set, behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] PR 2: a prospect who sends their own Calendly link gets the acknowledgement reply, the host gets the task and notification, and the thread turns booked when the event lands on the host calendar (preview, end to end).
- [ ] PR 2: if task creation fails, no reply is sent and the thread escalates as today.
- [ ] PR 2: the fallback-line split is stable per thread, and the follow-up results report shows bookings and replies for each half.
- [ ] Browser QA of the setting (save, validation error, suggestion from the knowledge base), with PostHog events verified landing.

## Open questions

* **Should the "or book here" line go on every offer, or be tested first?** Recommended default: test it 50/50 for 4 weeks. Our data shows follow-ups carrying non-booking links got about 13.5 points fewer replies, possibly a spam-filter effect. Booking-link follow-ups showed about 6 points fewer, but that is understated, because link bookings were never counted. Sending the link when the prospect *asks* is not in question and is on for everyone.
* **Who gets the "book via their link" task when the campaign has no host?** Recommended default: the deal owner, then the workspace owner.

## Implementation context

* Plan and research: AI SDR Follow-ups v2. Follow-up programme: ENG-14756.
* The earlier design for the prospect's-own-link reply, including the "only reply once the task exists" rule: ENG-11714, closed as a duplicate of ENG-11624, which only built the escalation.
* A meeting-type link also fixes the length mismatch in ENG-12059 when the meeting type and link agree.
* Exact files, rules, queries and tests are in this ticket's AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR scheduling leads without calendar connected and sending incorrect date messages
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Found Problem

The AI SDR is attempting to schedule appointments and send scheduling-related messages to leads even when the user's calendar is disconnected. This results in:

1. **Incorrect booking behavior**: Bot books appointments for times when the user is unavailable
2. **Confusing date messages**: Bot sent a message saying "the slot on the 29th was no longer available" when it was actually the 30th
3. **No calendar validation**: System allows scheduling to proceed without any connected calendar

## Reproduction Steps

1. User's calendar becomes disconnected (not reconnected)
2. AI SDR continues operating and communicating with leads
3. AI SDR attempts to schedule appointments without access to actual availability
4. Bot sends messages with incorrect/confusing date references
5. Bot successfully books appointments for times when user is not available
6. No calendar connection means no actual calendar integration, but bookings proceed anyway

## User Information

* **User:** Name 11
* **Reported:** January 31, 2025
* **Slack Thread:** <url:fegrowthpartner.slack.com>

## Expected Behavior

When calendar is disconnected:

1. AI SDR should detect the disconnection immediately
2. AI SDR should NOT attempt to schedule appointments without calendar access
3. AI SDR should either:
   * Pause scheduling functionality until calendar is reconnected
   * Show clear error/warning to user that calendar needs to be reconnected
   * Prevent any booking-related communications
4. Date references in messages should always be accurate and validated
5. No appointments should be booked without valid calendar connection

## Additional Context

User mentioned the email thread is "so hard to read" and difficult to troubleshoot - suggests there may be additional UI/UX issues with reviewing bot communications.

## Related Issues

* ENG-2348: Disable AI SDR until calendar connected (similar concept)
* ENG-2390: Multiple Users reporting calendar disconnecting
* ENG-2484: AI SDR meetings not syncing to Name 9 Calendar

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR continues attempting to schedule meetings after confirmation received
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Found Problem

The AI SDR is continuing to attempt scheduling additional meetings even after a lead has confirmed receipt of a meeting invitation and the meeting has been successfully scheduled. This results in:

1. **Redundant scheduling attempts**: AI SDR keeps trying to schedule meetings that are already scheduled
2. **Confusing lead experience**: Leads receive multiple scheduling messages after they've already confirmed
3. **No confirmation detection**: System doesn't recognize when a meeting invite has been sent and confirmed

## Reproduction Steps

1. AI SDR sends meeting invitation to lead (Name 21 - Interview Series Invitation)
2. Lead confirms they received the meeting invite ("I got it")
3. Meeting invitation is successfully sent and scheduled
4. AI SDR continues sending follow-up messages attempting to schedule the meeting
5. AI SDR doesn't recognize the meeting as confirmed/scheduled

## User Information

* **User/Lead:** Name 18 (lead email: <email>)
* **Campaign:** Interview Series Invitation
* **Reported by:** Name 17
* **Reported:** January 7, 2025
* **Slack Thread:** <url:fegrowthpartner.slack.com>

## Expected Behavior

When a meeting invitation is sent and lead confirms receipt:

1. AI SDR should detect that meeting invite was sent successfully
2. AI SDR should recognize lead's confirmation response ("I got it", "received", etc.)
3. AI SDR should NOT continue attempting to schedule the same meeting
4. AI SDR should transition to appropriate next conversation (meeting prep, confirmation, etc.)
5. System should mark the scheduling objective as "complete" once invitation is confirmed

## Screenshots

See attached screenshots in Slack thread showing the email sequence where:

* Meeting invite was sent
* Lead confirmed receipt
* AI SDR continued trying to schedule

## Additional Context

This impacts lead experience and may cause confusion or frustration. Related to scheduling logic and conversation state management.
